collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE III: DEFENSE, RAIDS AND THE FALLEN (LCC-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
"If anyone comes to raid our homeland, we'll be ready." Isola's people are peaceful but no pushovers: stamping dances and war chants, watch fires and plans, raids fended off or not, prisoners and bargains, and how the village honors those who defended it.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: During a raid alarm a child ran across the village to warn the elders: praise them, or scold them for the danger.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: When the conch blew last night, every child was supposed to run to the caves. (subject) did not. (subject.He/she) ran the other way, across the whole village, to wake the elders' hut, because the elders are a little deaf and did not hear the conch. It was a false alarm, in the end. (friend) is (subject.his/her) parent. What should (friend) do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (friend) hugs (subject) and tells (subject.him/her) it was brave, and also tells (subject.him/her) never, ever to do it again. The elders give (subject) a carved conch of (subject.his/her) own, so that next time they will be woken properly. (subject) sleeps with it.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) is so frightened that (friend.he/she) shouts. (subject) cries. Later, when (friend) has calmed down, (friend.he/she) sits on (subject)'s mat and explains that (friend.he/she) shouted because (friend.he/she) was scared, not because (subject) was bad. They make a new plan for the elders together.
